clue.text: Thieves select parcels, all with no middle and nothing in

indicators.note: the whole joined word loses its central letter, and in its place goes the nothing that comes in

parts.note: to pick is to select
packets are small parcels
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone describes thieves who choose hollow parcels with nothing inside them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all with no middle' acts on the whole of PICKPACKETS: its sixth, central letter A is dropped and 'nothing in' puts O in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickpockets are a kind of thief, stealing from people's pockets in crowds.

clue.text: Display in bar not very small to stand in

indicators.note: to stand in means to take a place within the remaining letters
not tells us the letter for very is taken away from the word for bar

parts.note: to bar is to prevent
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a stand-in at a bar, as if describing a pub's temporary barman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes V from PREVENT, leaving PREENT, and 'to stand in' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To present a thing is to display or show it.

clue.text: Gathers prosecutors will protect border

indicators.note: will protect says the prosecutors' letters surround the border, sheltering it

parts.note: CPS is the Crown Prosecution Service, the body that brings criminal prosecutions in England and Wales
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A news line: those who gather the prosecutors will guard the national frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The CPS, the Crown Prosecution Service, is England and Wales's public prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp fabric is to gather it into small folds or pleats.

clue.text: Request one by one making a good impression

parts.note: a plea is a request
singly means one at a time, one by one

explanation.surface: Asking people individually is a way of coming across well.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something pleasingly means doing it agreeably, so it makes a good impression.

clue.text: Swish vessel less ordinary

indicators.note: less says the letter for ordinary is taken out of the boat

parts.note: a canoe is a small boat, a vessel
O is a standard abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A smart boat, minus anything ordinary, sounds like an advert for a luxury craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swish' reads as an adjective meaning posh; here it is a noun, a whippy stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A swish is a thin switch or stick used for striking, as a cane is.

clue.text: Opponents in bridge contract appeal

parts.note: in bridge East and North sit on opposing sides, so E and N are opponents
a treaty is a formal contract between states

explanation.surface: At the bridge table, the rival pair makes an appeal over a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge partners are North-South and East-West, so E and N are on opposite sides.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request, an appeal for something.

clue.text: Swimmer no longer available to get cap

parts.note: a seal is a marine animal that swims
a dish that is off is no longer available on the menu

explanation.surface: A swimmer whose swimming cap has gone out of stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cap' looks like a swimming cap in this scene; it is a verb, to close the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap a well or pipe is to seal it off, closing it completely.

clue.text: Silly electronic currency units rising retrospectively

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
lire were the units of Italian currency
rising means going up

explanation.surface: A silly digital currency whose units are, looking back, going up in value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospectively' turns the whole of ELIREUP round.
explanation.definitionFit: Puerile behaviour is childish, and so foolish or silly.

clue.text: Hopeless deficits — I miss epic upturns, to some extent

indicators.note: upturns says the hidden letters are read backwards
to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gloomy pundit regrets that grand recoveries from deficits are now beyond them.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upturns' reads the hidden run CITSIMISSEP from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pessimistic person expects the worst, feeling there is no hope.

clue.text: 'Pint?' 'Very much so!'

definitions.meaning: offered a pint, a drinker might reply that it is not a half pint
British slang for very much, or absolutely

explanation.surface: A pub exchange: asked if they want a pint, the drinker eagerly agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British informal for 'and how!'; a pint is the full measure, not a half.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a pint is literally not a half, and the slang exclamation means emphatically yes.

clue.text: Acquaintance needing change of air housed by relatives accepting it

indicators.note: accepting means the relatives take the whole it-with-air group inside

parts.note: a family is a group of relatives

indicators.note: housed by puts the rearranged letters inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: change of says the letters of air are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting to know someone needs a change of scene, staying with relatives who accept it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is only a link; 'change of' is the anagram signal, not part of the definition, and the word 'it' in the clue is used as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Familiarity is close acquaintance or knowledge of a person or thing.

clue.text: Embarrassed seeing the woman's husband's framed record

indicators.note: framed means the record is set within the woman's letters, like a picture

parts.note: the woman's expands to she is
EP is an extended-play record
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: She is embarrassed to find her husband has had a record framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the woman's' is expanded to 'she is', not read as a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepish means showing embarrassment, typically from feeling foolish.

clue.text: Better scripture class

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject once called scripture
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a scripture class as a better option.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform something is to improve it, making it better — a verb sense.

clue.text: Shells found in farmer's furrows?

parts.note: a cart is a farmer's vehicle
ridges and furrows run side by side in a ploughed field

explanation.surface: Bomb shells unearthed in a farmer's ploughed field, read as a wartime find.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer names the ruts a farm cart leaves in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartridges are casings holding a charge and shot, the shells fired by guns.

clue.text: Cheers after most of football team scrap

indicators.note: after puts the thanks behind the team's letters

parts.note: a team is eleven players; most of it is ten, written 10, which looks like the letters I and O
ta is British informal for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Fans cheer once most of the side is scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The digits 10 are read as the letters IO: a team of eleven with one sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota, the smallest Greek letter, means a tiny amount, a scrap.

clue.text: Cheating, in a huff until rehabilitated

indicators.note: rehabilitated means restored to a new state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone caught cheating sulks until they are back in favour.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfaithful partner is one who cheats on the other.

clue.text: Criminal scared to admit this person was a squealer

indicators.note: to admit means the rearranged letters let me in
criminal means wrongly done, so the letters of scared are rearranged

parts.note: this person is the setter, me

explanation.surface: A frightened criminal confessed, turning informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' is the anagram signal, making SCREAD; 'to admit' takes in the setter. 'Squealer' suggests an informer but means one who shrieks.
explanation.definitionFit: Screamed means shrieked, as a squealer does with high, piercing cries.

clue.text: One's been chilly — I stay, oddly, showing foolishness

parts.note: one is becomes I am, shortened to I'm

indicators.note: oddly means taking the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Someone has been cold but is staying put, which strikes others as foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the odd letters across 'been chilly I stay' to give BECILITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbecility is stupidity, utter foolishness.

clue.text: Pirate wields cudgel to obstruct rising? On the contrary

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters rise, read from the bottom up
wields means the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A pirate uses a club to stop an uprising, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run sits in 'cudGEL TO OBstruct' and is read backwards, upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg as a verb means to make or sell illicit copies, which is what pirating means.

clue.text: Business degree causes deep sleep

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Studying for a business degree sends someone into a deep sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A coma is a prolonged state of deep unconsciousness.

clue.text: Constantly working with side at Old Trafford?

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
and means along with
on is the leg side in cricket, and Old Trafford is a Test cricket ground in Manchester

explanation.surface: A footballer plays nonstop with the Manchester United side at Old Trafford.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford is a famous football stadium but also the Lancashire cricket ground; in cricket the on side is the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: On and on is an idiom for continuing without stopping.

clue.text: Set up second form for, say, reading breaks on vessel

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: breaks means the letter for reading cuts into the vessel

parts.note: a wok is a cooking vessel
reading is one of the three Rs, so R stands for it

explanation.surface: A sign-up instruction for a second form, with reading interrupting work on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter confirmed 'for' belongs to the definition. 'breaks' puts R inside WOK.
explanation.definitionFit: To rework something is to revise it, giving it a new or second version.

clue.text: One may turn over a bit in bed

definitions.text: One may turn over a bit in bed

parts.words: One may turn over a bit in bed
parts.note: the surface suggests a restless sleeper; the bed is a flower bed and the bit turned over is soil

explanation.surface: Someone tossing and turning in bed at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's hand tool is used to dig and turn over small amounts of earth in a border.

clue.text: It's in Lear — changing it upset them?

indicators.note: it's in means the word it goes inside the other letters
upset turns the rearranged letters over, reading them backwards
changing says the letters of Lear and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rewriting King Lear would upset the scholars who know it best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes ITAREL, 'upset' turns it to LERATI, and the first It goes inside; 'them' are those who would be upset by changing Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are the literary, educated people who would be upset by tampering with Shakespeare.

clue.text: Beginner's mistake, trading bits of public relations

indicators.note: trading bits of means one word's opening letter is swapped for the other's

parts.note: a typo is a typing mistake
first letter of public
first letter of relations

explanation.surface: A novice's blunder in public relations work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trading bits of' swaps P, the start of 'public', for R, the start of 'relations'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a novice, someone just starting to learn.

clue.text: Libel about US city restricting Scottish smoker

indicators.note: restricting means the about and city letters hem in the chimney

parts.note: ca is circa, Latin for about
NY is New York
lum is Scots for a chimney, which smokes

explanation.surface: A libel suit about a city where a Scot's smoking was restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoker' suggests a person but is a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is a false and damaging statement, the kind libel law addresses.

clue.text: How some greet carefree housing cheat given party backing

indicators.note: housing means carefree holds the rest inside

parts.note: gay in its older sense means carefree

indicators.note: backing means the combined letters are read in reverse
given means the cheat takes the party in

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A carefree host welcomes a fraudster to a party in support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' puts one DO in the other, making DDOO, and 'backing' turns that to OODD before 'housing' encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-day is a greeting, said on meeting someone in parts of the English-speaking world.

clue.text: Man's condition after creation of gardens — OK, shattered

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After Eden's gardens were made, man fell from grace: everything shattered.
explanation.walkthrough: The scene is the Garden of Eden: after the Fall, mankind was abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Godforsaken means abandoned by God, the state of fallen humanity in Genesis.
